title: End-to-end hybrid scenario walkthrough
hook: This walkthrough connects an on-premises data center to multiple AWS Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) through Direct Connect with VPN backup into a Transit Gateway, adds VPC endpoints for private AWS API access, and consumes a SaaS fraud API through PrivateLink — the story interviewers want instead of isolated definitions.

blocks.text: Imagine a retailer: ERP runs on-premises, microservices live in prod, staging, and shared-services VPCs. Direct Connect is primary hybrid path; VPN backs it up. Transit Gateway segments prod from staging while allowing both to reach shared services. Each VPC gets an S3 Gateway endpoint and STS Interface endpoint. Prod consumes a fraud-detection SaaS through PrivateLink — no internet egress for scoring calls.

entries.plainDefinition: On-premises and AWS resources connected by private or VPN links.
Segmentation boundary on Transit Gateway controlling inter-spoke reachability.
entries.example: Staging RT has no route to prod CIDR.

entries.plainDefinition: Only AWS prefixes use DX/VPN; general internet exits locally from data center.

blocks.text: Senior interviews ask for end-to-end designs with failure modes, not flashcards. This scenario shows when to pick each Module 06 tool and how they compose. It mirrors real migration programs: hybrid connectivity first, hub segmentation, then endpoint hardening, then SaaS PrivateLink.

blocks.title: Design checklist
blocks.body: Hybrid HA path, TGW segmentation, AWS API privacy via endpoints, SaaS via PrivateLink, observability, documented failover RTO.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Hybrid ingress
items.body: DX Private VIF → Direct Connect Gateway → TGW. VPN backup with lower BGP preference.

items.title: Segment spokes
items.body: Prod and staging associated with separate TGW RTs; static route to shared-services only where needed.

items.title: Private AWS APIs
items.body: S3 Gateway + STS Interface endpoints in every VPC; Lambda workers skip NAT for artifacts and credentials.

items.title: SaaS fraud API
items.body: PrivateLink Interface endpoint in prod VPC only; staging uses mock until cutover.

items.title: Failover drill
items.body: Withdraw DX routes in maintenance window; verify VPN telemetry UP and batch jobs retry successfully.

diagram.title: End-to-end hybrid reference
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  OP[On-prem ERP] --> DX[Direct Connect primary]
  OP --> VPN[VPN backup]
  DX --> TGW[Transit Gateway]
  VPN --> TGW
  TGW --> PROD[Prod VPC]
  TGW --> STG[Staging VPC]
  TGW --> SHR[Shared services VPC]
  PROD --> S3EP[S3 Gateway endpoint]
  PROD --> PL[PrivateLink SaaS]
  SHR --> AD[Directory services]

snippet.label: CloudFormation — DX gateway to TGW with allowed prefixes
snippet.code:
DxGatewayAssociation:
  Type: AWS::DirectConnect::GatewayAssociation
  Properties:
    DirectConnectGatewayId: !Ref DxGateway
    GatewayId: !Ref HubTgw
    AllowedPrefixes:
      - 10.10.0.0/16
      - 10.20.0.0/16
      - 10.50.0.0/16
snippet.explanation: Advertise only required VPC CIDRs to on-prem — avoid summarizing entire 10.0.0.0/8 if segmentation matters on-prem too.

snippet.label: CLI — verify TGW hybrid routes
snippet.explanation: Confirm on-prem prefix via DX/VPN attachment and shared-services static route appear in prod RT.

snippet.label: CLI — roll out S3 Gateway endpoints
snippet.code:
for RTB in $(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-prod --query 'RouteTables[].RouteTableId' --output text); do
  aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-prod --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 --route-table-ids $RTB
done
snippet.explanation: Automate consistent Gateway endpoint coverage during migration waves.

snippet.label: CLI — failover drill monitoring
snippet.code:
while true; do
  aws ec2 describe-vpn-connections --query 'VpnConnections[].VgwTelemetry[*].[OutsideIpAddress,Status]' --output text
  sleep 5
done
snippet.explanation: During DX maintenance, watch both VPN tunnels before withdrawing DX BGP announcements.

blocks.title: Migration runtime behavior
rows: DX → TGW → VPC with S3 endpoint
AWS SDK v3 needs retry logic on failover
Staging may still call public mock API
OpenTelemetry does not show missing TGW routes

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Migrating apps before TGW routes exist. Single TGW RT propagating all attachments — staging reaches prod. Testing only DX happy path, never VPN failover.

blocks.text: Document separate RTO for DX versus VPN convergence — batch jobs need idempotent retries. Physical DX redundancy requires two connections, often to different DX locations. How to prove it in production: quarterly failover with BGP table capture; compare DataSync throughput DX vs VPN; alarm on TunnelState and DX ConnectionState; run game day where staging must not reach prod CIDR per Flow Logs.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Hybrid diagram with VPN only and no segmentation or endpoints. Strong answer: name hub, backup path, route domains, private AWS APIs, PrivateLink for SaaS, and tested failover.

interviewTakeaways: Reference: on-prem → DX primary + VPN backup → TGW → segmented VPC spokes.
Route domains isolate prod/staging; shared services via static TGW routes only.
VPC endpoints per spoke for S3/STS; PrivateLink for third-party SaaS in prod.
60s: DX+VPN to TGW. Segment RTs. Endpoints for AWS APIs. PrivateLink for SaaS. BGP failover drill quarterly. Flow Logs prove isolation.
Follow-up: what breaks if on-prem advertises overly broad 10.0.0.0/8?
commonPitfalls: Hybrid design without backup VPN — senior interviewers reject single-path hybrid.
Strong answer: DX primary, VPN secondary, BGP, TGW segmentation, endpoints, tested failover.
Shared-services RT propagated to all attachments — staging reaches prod CIDR.
On-prem firewall permits 10.0.0.0/8 — bypasses intended TGW segmentation.

jsTsCorrelations.note: On-prem Node processes use DX for S3 after endpoint cutover; implement exponential backoff when VPN failover causes transient SDK errors.
TypeScript deployment pipelines switch internal ALB DNS while TGW routes must already exist — infrastructure-first ordering like database migrations before code.
